review_criteria.name: Substantial contribution to language processing
review_criteria.official_explanation: ARR papers are held to *CL main-conference standards, not generic ML standards.
review_criteria.quote: the submissions are expected to make a substantial contribution to computational processing of human language

review_criteria.name: Technically sound and appropriately scoped
review_criteria.official_explanation: Soundness and scope are stated as the minimum bar for published research.
review_criteria.quote: Above all else, published research should at least be technically sound and appropriately scoped.

review_criteria.name: Novelty claims must be backed by references
review_criteria.official_explanation: A reviewer alleging lack of novelty must supply a reference.
review_criteria.quote: If the paper claims e.g. a novel method, and you think you've seen this before - you need to provide a reference

review_criteria.name: Sufficient evidence for the claim made
review_criteria.official_explanation: Extra experiments are not required beyond what the claim needs.
review_criteria.quote: a paper only needs to present sufficient evidence for the claim that the authors are making

review_criteria.name: Complete assumptions and proofs
review_criteria.official_explanation: Formal contributions must state assumptions and carry complete proofs.
review_criteria.quote: All assumptions should be clearly stated. If the paper contributes formal statements (theorems, propositions, lemmas, corollaries), they should be supported by complete and correct proofs.

review_criteria.name: Enough detail to reproduce experiments
review_criteria.official_explanation: Reviewers assess whether details and code suffice for reproducibility.
review_criteria.quote: Are there enough details to reproduce the experiments, including hyperparameter selection?

review_criteria.name: Many kinds of contribution are in scope
review_criteria.official_explanation: The reviewer guidelines reject methodology-preference heuristics.
review_criteria.quote: NLP is an interdisciplinary field, relying on many kinds of contributions: models, resource, survey, data/linguistic/social analysis, position, and theory.

mandatory_policy.statement: Long papers may use up to 8 content pages and short papers up to 4; exceeding the length requirements or omitting the Limitations section is desk rejection.
mandatory_policy.quote: Submissions that exceed the length requirements, or are missing a limitations section, will be desk rejected.

mandatory_policy.statement: A dedicated Limitations section is required in both long and short papers.
mandatory_policy.quote: Authors are required to discuss the limitations of their work in a dedicated section titled “Limitations”.

mandatory_policy.statement: ARR precludes multiple submissions; a paper under review elsewhere cannot be submitted and an ARR submission cannot go elsewhere during review.
mandatory_policy.quote: ARR precludes multiple submissions. ARR will not consider any paper that is under review in a journal or another conference at the time of submission, and submitted papers must not be submitted elsewhere during the ARR review period.

mandatory_policy.statement: Papers must not include authors’ names and affiliations.
mandatory_policy.quote: Papers must not include authors’ names and affiliations.

mandatory_policy.statement: Generative AI use for writing or coding, and its scope, must be disclosed in the Responsible NLP Checklist.
mandatory_policy.quote: Their use for writing or coding, as well as its scope, must be disclosed in the Responsible NLP Checklist.

recommended_practice.statement: ARR encourages supplementary appendices, software and data for reproducibility.
recommended_practice.quote: ARR encourages the submission of these supplementary materials to improve the reproducibility of results and to enable authors to provide additional information that does not fit in the paper.

recommended_practice.statement: Authors are recommended to locate revisions by section and line numbers.
recommended_practice.quote: It is recommended to refer to the location of revisions using section and line numbers.

recommended_practice.statement: Reviews should be professional and neutral, if not kind.
recommended_practice.quote: Above all, a good review should be professional and neutral, if not kind.

compliance_checks.requirement: Dedicated Limitations section present before the references in both long and short papers.
Long papers at most 8 content pages; short papers at most 4 content pages, excluding limitations, ethics and references.
No author names or affiliations; self-references do not reveal identity; supplementary material anonymized.
Generative AI writing/coding use disclosed in the Responsible NLP Checklist.
Confirm the paper is not under review elsewhere and is not an undisclosed resubmission.

changes_from_prior_year.change: ACL adopted a sustainable reviewing policy that applies from October 2026: review is capped to capacity, submissions need a qualified service contributor, and author and first-author submission caps apply.
ARR moved from 8-week to 10-week cycles beginning with the May 2025 cycle and now runs about five cycles per year.
The ARR author and reviewer guidelines state they will be updated after the August 2026 cycle to match the sustainable reviewing policy.

unknown_policies.question: Which named ARR cycle does the standing call for papers text govern?
unknown_policies.reason: ARR is a rolling venue and its call for papers is a standing document that does not map its rules to one named cycle. The October 2026 cycle is recorded in a separate profile; per-cycle dates are not inferred from the standing text.

unknown_policies.question: Do the posted reviewer guidelines still govern the October 2026 cycle?
unknown_policies.reason: The reviewer guidelines page states that the current version applies until the August 2026 review cycle and will be updated afterwards to match the sustainable reviewing policy. Retrieved 2026-10-10, the page does not confirm whether the posted text is already the updated version.

unknown_policies.question: Do the posted author guidelines reflect the October 2026 sustainable reviewing policy?
unknown_policies.reason: The author guidelines page carries the same notice as the reviewer guidelines: the text will be updated after the August 2026 cycle. The CFP has already been updated, but the guidelines pages have not been confirmed as updated.

unknown_policies.question: How does the review lottery select submissions without a guaranteed service contributor?
unknown_policies.reason: The call states such submissions will be considered via a lottery and may be desk rejected, but does not state lottery timing, odds or ordering.
